To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed mass ratios of charged fermions and neutrinos determine the mixing matrices in a model independent way, and that this is the case despite the strong hierarchy in the neutrino masses and mixing.
the observed quark and leponic mixing matrices can be simultaneously understood from the observed mass hierarchy pattern of the three fermion generations.

(i) the observed pattern of quark and leon mixing is a consequence of the observed pattern of the fermion mass hierarchies; and (ii) the observed pattern in the fermion mass hierarchy can be understood as a result of the breaking of a minimal flavor symmetry that is consistent with the observed pattern of fermion mixing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the double mass hierarchy pattern in the fermion spectrum.
the question of whether the observed mixing patterns in quarks and leptonic sectors are consistent with a double mass hierarchy.
the question of whether the observed hierarchically ordered fermionic masses and mixing angles are accidental or not.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed quark and leptonic mixing angles are determined by the observed fermion mass ratios.
the quark and leptonic mixing matrices are fully determined by the four mass ratios in the two sectors.

the observed hierarchically ordered mass spectra of quarks and leptonic masses, and the large mixing angles in the lepton sector, can be understood in a simple way, without any need for additional structure in the mass matrices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in a minimal flavor symmetry framework, we are able to understand the observed mass hierarchies in both quarks and charged leptons, the mixing patterns of both sectors and predict the lightest neutrinos mass to be well below 0. 01 eV.
, in the double mass hierarchy pattern, the quark and the lepton mixing patterns can be simultaneously understood.
the double mass hierarchy pattern is a natural consequence of the observed mass hierarchies and it simultaneously provides a consistent description of the fermionic mixing matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if the masses of the three neutrino generations satisfy the hierarchy m 3 > m 2 > m 1, then the mixing angles of the leptonic sector are determined by the mass ratios of the charged leptons.
the double hierarchy pattern in the fermion masses can be used to simultaneously describe the observed patterns of the quark and the lepton mixing.

the double mass hierarchy pattern in the fermionic sector, i.e. the two strong hierachies m 3 / m 2 ≳ 10 and m 2 / m 1 ≳ 10, is a sufficient condition for the observed mixing pattern of quarks and leptos.
